werust docs — a static site, addressed by its hash

The content-addressed floor

A real static docs site, generated by a static site generator and pinned to a CID, opened as a first-class page by the native path.

This page is fetched by its content identifier, not by trusting an origin. The bytes are verified against their hash on the way in, and only then rendered: a mismatch does not render. This is where the thesis lands first — a verifiable, content-addressed document rendered at parity with the served web.

What the floor proves

The same native T1 path that renders a served article renders this content-addressed site identically: real WHATWG parse, a core-CSS cascade, and properly shaped Latin text. As the ladder puts it:

A tier is not reached until BOTH floors land: the server-web floor AND the content-addressed floor.

Inside the T1 static scope

  • Headings, paragraphs, lists, links, and inline emphasis.
  • A core-CSS stylesheet: colour, typography, and normal flow.
  • No floats, flexbox, grid, or tables — that is a later tier.
  • No JavaScript — that is a later tier too.

Verification moves to the hash: the origin need not be trusted.
